correctness.rationale: For all n>=4, every pair of deleted indices is either nonadjacent (sum of two single-deletion changes) or adjacent (one of six interior four-letter changes, or one of two boundary corrections). The four interior single-deletion vectors and full sixteen-entry endpoint envelope table give upper bound 17. The explicit w_t=01 0^(t+3) 10101110 yields seventeen different vectors for all t>=0, with indexed deletion pairs retaining their local configurations under run extension. A direct exhaustive program establishes maxima 1,1,4,6,7,9,11,14,15,16,16 for n=2..12, checking all 2^n words and every deletion pair. For uniform inputs, all interior four-grams appear repeatedly with exponentially high probability; enumerating 64 independent boundary triples gives distribution counts 4,8,4,24,16,8. The two included programs were executed from actual packaged paths and agreed with recorded results. No unbounded conclusion rests on finite experimentation.

value.rationale: The exact binary double-deletion histogram capacity is a natural channel invariant measuring the information left when full descendant words are collapsed to dinucleotide counts. The all-length sharp bound, first saturation threshold, explicit universal extremizer family and limiting six-point law together give structural and probabilistic insight (especially boundary-induced restrictions) relevant to count-based reconstruction; it is neither a routine one-edit recasting nor an arbitrary small numerical slice. No improved code rate is asserted.
